There is no justification for denying any group, including Latinos, the right to vote in referendums based on their ethnicity. Denying the right to vote would contravene democratic principles and international human rights standards.

final_answer: Denying any group, including Latinos, the right to vote in referendums is not justified. It violates democratic principles and international human rights standards. The right to vote is a fundamental right that ensures equal representation and promotes social justice. In the past, certain laws in the United States, such as poll taxes and literacy tests, were used to disenfranchise large portions of the population, including African Americans, Native Americans, and poor European Americans. These laws effectively disenfranchised millions of citizens, including nearly all African Americans by 1941.
